newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus's opposition join forces for elections.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus's opposition join forces for elections.

text.p: Leaders of Cyprus's three largest opposition parties agreed on Thursday to field a common candidate to contest the island's presidential elections due in early 1998.

"We have reached an agreement on the basic programming issues," said Vassos Lyssarides, president of the socialist Edek party after meeting with the leaders of the communist Akel party and the centre-left United Democrats.
"The agreement is of course subject to the approval of the collective organs in each party," he added.
Nicosia lawyer Marios Eliades, a moderate pro-European, is widely touted as being the opposition's candidate in the elections, which are due by the end of February 1998.
Presidential elections are held every five years on the eastern Mediterranean island.
The three parties polled around 44.5 percent of the vote between them during parliamentary elections, which are also held every five years, in May 1996.

Incumbent president, right wing Glafcos Clerides who was elected in February 1993, has kept the public guessing on whether he will run for the presidency again. He says he will make his decision known in the latter part of this year.
